text: I'd say in a numerical sequence
So for this image for example, the airport must have at least 28 runways?

Runways are usually numbered according to their direction, more precisely called runway magnetic bearing or QFU. Consider a plane flying toward the runway on final approach in a day without any wind. Divide its magnetic heading by 10, round it to the nearest whole number and you'll usually get the runway number.
Thus assignment + taxiing becomes easier based on routes
28 means 280 degrees on the compass. same runway on the other side would be 8 (for 80 degrees)
and if you have two runways in parallel, the one on the left gets the letter L (28L) and the other would be 28R
